pr_title: [Backport v2.7-branch] Bluetooth: Host: L2CAP collision mitigation
pr_comments: @carlescufi, @hermabe - does this need to be backported?

@cfriedt I am not sure it is needed on the 2.7 branch. The API for connecting EATT channels is not public and there is thus no way for the application to initiate connections of EATT channels. Responding to incoming EATT connection requests is supported on 2.7. A collision only occurs if both devices initiate EATT connection at the same time.

Unless the other EATT work being done on main now is also to be backported, I don't see the need for the collision mitigation on 2.7.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: EATT bearer L2CAP collision mitigation
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

BT Core Spec:
"If both devices request L2CAP connections (on EATT PSM) simultaneously and both devices
have limited resources, a device may reject the incoming request and find its
own request is also rejected. In this situation, the Central may retry
immediately but the Peripheral shall wait a minimum of 100 ms before retrying;
on LE connections, the Peripheral shall wait at least 2 ×
(connPeripheralLatency + 1) × connInterval if that is longer."

While spec is not requiring any specific behavior when collision occurs (other than not retrying too soon by peripheral), test specification requires that peripheral IUT re-try after mentioned timeout.


**Describe the solution you'd like**
Collision should be detected and either host should retry connection on L2CAP channel or notify application about it.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
None.

**Additional context**
This is affecting L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C qualification test case.
comments:
Some comments on this issue:
 -  since this is a GATT requirement on EATT PSM (and not L2CAP protocol one) it should be implemented in GATT/ATT code (ie not directly visible for application, and not implemented in L2CAP code)
 - I think we could have generic timer for establishing EATT as peripheral and then it can also be reused by collision handling
 - in GATT/ATT we can have simple counter on how many retries
 - timer can be possibly randomized (eg min_time + some rand) to improve IOP

Im curious about how we come to the conclusion it is a GATT requirement? L2CAP/TIM/BV-03-C seem to be L2CAP specific as well, that said I don't see any new error that can be used for collision detection or the stack is supposed to detect this based on the ongoing connection matching the PSM and checking if all channels are refused with 0x0004 (Connection refused – no resources available) on the response? It would have been a lot clearer if a new error was introduced that way both stacks can confirm a collision has been detected and the retry procedure can start.

review_comments:
I have concerns about the logic in `ecred_connect_cb`.

-
  If the outgoing connect is rejected first and then the incoming connect is rejected, the `att_schedule_eatt_connect` is called with the `attempted_to_connect - succeeded_to_connect` from the incoming request. It should be the values from the outgoing request.
 Example scenario:
  - Send L2CAP connect with 4 channels requested (because CONFIG_BT_EATT_MAX = 3).
  - Receive reject (Reason is relevant, but e.g. because the remote has allocated the channels for the next request, but not yet sent the request).
  - Receive L2CAP connect with 5 channels requested.
  - Send reject (because ATT_CHAN_MAX = CONFIG_BT_EATT_MAX).
  - Schedule a retry asking for 5 channels. (This is a bug.)

- Two outgoing EATT connects that are both rejected will trigger the retry. This is not too bad, but it's not the intention.

- This `ecred_connect_cb` handler will catch rejects for ecred connect request not related to EATT. Two rejects will trigger an unwanted eatt_connect.
  Example scenario:
   - Application tries to create a ecred connectiont to an unrelated PSM.
   - It's rejected.
   - Application tries again.
   - It's rejected again.
   - This spuriously triggers an `att_schedule_eatt_connect`.

This is not a problem with the back port. But we may want to create a new issue for this.

@alwa-nordic this is a backport of an existing PR, https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/42268. Let's discuss with @hermabe whether this requires additional changes in `main` or we can merge this backport.

I think all of these are valid bugs.
1. Yes, instead of counting attempted and succeeded channels we should use the `ident` that is set on each channel when a request is sent.
2. I think this can be solved by having separate callbacks for request and response. Maybe something nicer using `ident` can be done.
3. The `psm` of the channel should be checked. This is only a requirement on the EATT PSM, all other shall be ignored.

I made some changes that seem to fix these issues. Please take a look: https://github.com/hermabe/zephyr/commit/dfd454f585b60d9bce30225775b18c2637cce9b6

It is not the nicest, but seems to work.
